_meta.description: Ethiopian crop x season advisory nitrogen targets. P/K/pH are season-independent baseline bands; only the N target changes between Meher and Belg. These are advisory targets, not measured soil observations, and must not be used as supervised training rows.
_meta.review_note: Compiled from the user-supplied Enhancement D seasonal matrix (2026). Verify crop/season ranges and operational notes against EIAR, regional research centers and local extension guidance before presenting them as official recommendations.
_meta.default_semantics: N is season-specific. P/K/pH are static; the stored baseline bands are used only when no more specific variety/zone band exists.
sources: User-supplied Enhancement D seasonal agronomic optimum matrix (2026)

meher.label: Meher (main rainy season)
meher.note: Long rainy season with sustained moisture and a longer crop growth window. Nitrogen targets are higher; split urea to reduce leaching.

belg.label: Belg (short rains)
belg.note: Short, erratic rains with a compressed growth window. Lower the N target to avoid excessive vegetative growth and moisture stress; P/K/pH stay unchanged.

meher.note: Long-maturing hybrids (e.g. BH-660) use maximum N over 5-6 months; split urea applications.

belg.note: Short-duration open-pollinated varieties. Higher N risks moisture-stress failure before grain filling.

meher.note: Main bread-wheat season. Split-apply urea to reduce leaching from Kiremt rains.

belg.note: Only select highland pockets (e.g. Bale). The lower yield ceiling limits N utility.

wheat.source: User-supplied Enhancement D seasonal agronomic optimum matrix (2026)

meher.note: High-yielding white varieties such as Kuncho. High N during Meher rains increases lodging risk.

belg.note: Rare, short-cycle mixed teff. Keep N low to avoid rapid vegetative drying.

meher.note: Long-duration varieties planted in Belg but harvested in Meher span both seasons.

belg.note: Short-cycle varieties planted for a fast Belg turnaround in lowland zones.

meher.note: Heavy hilling protects top-dressed urea from leaching during intense rains.

belg.note: Shorter tuber-initiation window; ensure basal nutrients are readily accessible.

meher.note: Main grain-legume window. Rely primarily on biological nitrogen fixation; starter N only.

belg.note: Lower humidity reduces active nodulation; keep starter N low.
